newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan key panel urges broad deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Japan key panel urges broad deregulation.

text.p: A subcommittee drawing up deregulation steps for Japan's financial markets on Thursday called for a broad range of reforms to revitalise the nation's economy, committee officials said.
A final report submitted by the group to the Administrative Reform Committee is likely to be sent to Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto later this month.
The report is expected to form the core of new deregulation measures Hashimoto plans to announce next March.
It calls for broad reform and deregulation in the areas of land, agriculture, telecommunications, transport, energy, finance, employment, medicine and education.

Proposals in the report in the six areas of finance, information technology, distribution, land, employment and medicine were almost in line with reforms that the Economic Council, another advisory panel, recommended last month.
Regarding transport, Thursday's report called for abolition of rules limiting establishment of new airline routes and air fares.

The report remained vague about a price-setting mechanism for books, newspapers, magazines and compact discs which allows newspaper companies and publishers to set the same prices for their products. The report merely called for a review of the price-setting mechanism for printed material.
The report also said rules restricting establishment of holding companies must be abolished as soon as possible.
In the area of financial deregulation, the report suggested sales channels for insurance products and investment trusts be expanded by allowing sales of such items at banks.
